content: Certain glucose-lowering medications exhibit direct protective effects on the kidneys that extend beyond their role in glycemic control. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, for example, decrease renal tubular glucose reabsorption, lower blood pressure, and reduce albuminuria. These effects collectively contribute to a slower decline in glomerular filtration rate (GFR). Additionally, SGLT2 inhibitors mitigate oxidative stress and inflammation within kidney tissues, further supporting renal health. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists also provide protective effects for the kidneys. However, the renoprotective mechanisms of GLP-1 receptor agonists are less comprehensively studied compared to those of SGLT2 inhibitors. When selecting glucose-lowering therapies, it is essential to consider both cardiovascular and renal benefits, particularly in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD).
